sections.heading: Hail Last Night, a Letter This Week, and No Idea What Comes Next
body: Picture the morning after a bad storm. You can see a few shingles in the yard, and a neighbor already has a ladder against his house. Your insurance company has sent a form, and you don't know what the adjuster looks for or who is supposed to tell you the next step.
This is the moment to call someone who has already walked other Peoria homeowners through it. Nobody should have to learn roofing and insurance in the same week.

Your Peoria page has a clear headline, "Roofing Contractor in Peoria, IL". Your About page is 119 words with no headline of its own, and every service sits on one 251-word page.

Your customers fill in what the site leaves out. They write about Amanda explaining the claim, Jose looking at the roof and a yard left clean. Your site doesn't tell the claim walk-through or the clean-up story in your customers' words.

On a phone it is worse: each page runs more than three times wider than the screen, so people scroll sideways to read it. We built a site around what your customers already say, with Amanda on the claim, Jose on the roof and a page of its own for roof replacement.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Roofer People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page: what your site does today and what we changed.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn who you are and where you work.
problems: On a phone the page runs more than three times wider than the screen, so people scroll sideways to read it, and many leave.
Your Peoria page shows five testimonials, but the claim walk-through and the clean-up your Google reviews describe aren't told in your customers' words.
fixes: A page that fits a phone, with the call button one tap away.
A headline that says roofer in Peoria, IL, right at the top, followed by the claim walk-through your customers describe.
cards.alsoAdd: Every page set up behind the scenes so Google and AI tools like ChatGPT know exactly what you do, where you work, and what your customers say.

cards.title: Roof Replacement
cards.why: Your biggest job, and today it shares one short page with six other things.
problems: Roofing, siding, metal roofs, gutters, the warranty and storm damage all sit on one 251-word page, so no page is about roof replacement in Peoria.
The headline on that page names Peoria and the services as a group, not the one job people search for.
fixes: One page for roof replacement in Peoria, IL: the claim, the steps and the gutters and siding that go with it.
Reviews placed beside the part of the job they describe.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a homeowner with a leak or a letter from the insurance company decides to call.
problems: Your contact block shows (309) 567-8236, while the Call or Text button dials 309-316-3652, so two callers can reach two different lines.
Contact in your menu goes to the home page instead of a page of its own.
fixes: A contact page with one number that matches your Google listing, plus your address, hours and email.
A short list of what to have ready when you call.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already describe how you work: Jose on the roof, Amanda on the claim, a clean yard at the end. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we'll walk you through this demo and plan your new site.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your contact block and your Google listing show (309) 567-8236, while your Call or Text button dials (309) 316-3652, so which number is live, and who answers each one? This demo uses the Google number.
Your About page says BBB A+ accredited, while we found no BBB profile for you, so is the accreditation current, and should it go on your listings?
A search result for your Angi listing says you don't offer emergency service, while your site says nothing either way, so what should every listing say about after-hours calls?

offer.heading: The offer we'd build with you
offer.text: This is a proposal for you to decide on, not something JG Roofing does today. It is a one-page claim and job timeline, handed to the homeowner before the tear-off, with each step in order. As far as we found, none of the three competitor sites we could read offers one.
points: Amanda already explains the claim step by step. Put the steps on one page the homeowner keeps: the adjuster visit, what the insurance company sends, and who to call with a question.
Add the date, the timeframe and the cleanup on the same page, so the week of the work holds no surprises.
Say plainly what the page leaves out: coverage and settlement belong to the insurance company. Terms are yours to set.
